issues.claim: Calendar booking (Google Calendar) integration cost: "Google states that all standard use of the Calendar API is available at no additional cost" (integrations entry, and again in running_costs 'Scheduling ... $0 in licence fees').
issues.problem: Overstated paraphrase. The cited quota page does not say "all standard use ... at no additional cost"; it says usage under a 1,000,000-request/day per-project threshold "doesn't incur extra charges", that billing details will be shared later in 2026 with 90 days' notice, and that quotas changed on May 1, 2026. The $0 conclusion is still right at pilot volume (a few hundred requests a month), so no number is wrong - only the attribution.
issues.fix: Reword to: "no charge below Google's 1,000,000 requests/day billing threshold; Google states full billing details will follow later in 2026", and drop the phrase "all standard use".

issues.problem: Misstates the vendor's entry price. The DigitalOcean Droplet page lists Basic Droplets from $4.00/mo (512 MiB) and $6.00/mo (1 GiB); $12.00 is the 2 GiB size. The plan's own running-cost row is correct ("$12-$24", basis lists $6/$12/$24), so this is a wording error in one bullet, not in the cost model.
issues.fix: Change to "DigitalOcean Basic Droplets from $6/month, with the plan sizing at $12-$24/month".

issues.claim: Running costs: phase 2 voice "about $26 per month for 300 minutes at the cheapest published configuration".
issues.problem: Two small imprecisions, neither changing the decision: (a) $0.055 infra + $0.015 platform voice + $0.0032 LLM + $0.015 telephony = $0.0882/min x 300 = ~$26.46, which excludes the $2.00/mo Retell number mentioned in the same basis (so ~$28.4 all-in); (b) Claude 5.5 Haiku at $0.0032/min is not the cheapest published LLM on the Retell page (GPT 5 nano is $0.0016/min), so "cheapest published configuration" is not strictly accurate.
issues.fix: Say "about $26-29/month for 300 minutes including the $2 number, using Claude 5.5 Haiku at $0.0032/min; cheaper LLM options exist and the published overall range is $0.07-$0.31/min".

issues.claim: Integrations, Anthropic Claude API: method includes "no training on client data", cited to platform.claude.com pricing page.
issues.problem: The cited pricing page says nothing about training or data use, so this supporting claim is unattributed. (The Messages API and all three per-MTok prices on that page are correct.)
issues.fix: Either cite Anthropic's data-usage/privacy page for the training statement or move it to the risk/mitigation section as an unverified vendor representation to confirm in the DPA.

issues.claim: Feasibility block (technical_1_5 4, commercial_1_5 3, weeks_to_pilot, founder_days in each build phase).
issues.problem: suggested_pricing is labelled inference throughout, but the feasibility scores and the per-phase founder_days carry no inline inference label (founder-days are only covered generically in caveats). Scores and effort are the consultancy's judgement, not sourced numbers.
issues.fix: Tag the feasibility block and each founder_days value as inference, e.g. "founder_days: 3-4 (inference)" and "feasibility: inference based on the two unconfirmed integration gates".

issues.claim: Business facts about Fraser Brothers used as the premise (17 staff, Edison 8:15-4:15 / Belford close 5:00 / Tinton Falls 4:30, three published office numbers, ~10 commercial niches, ~40 carrier appointments, crm.bridge.insure upload link).
issues.problem: Not verifiable from any page either the author or I can open: fraserbrothers.com/contact returns only Agency Revolution boilerplate and a copyright line, and /claims-center behaves the same; the homepage does render and is consistent with "quote/contact forms only, no booking or chat widget", but does not carry hours or headcount. The plan discloses this in caveats and in current_tools, so it is not presented as sourced - it remains an open risk for the value case.
issues.fix: Get the principal (or a Google Business Profile / site JSON-LD) to confirm hours, phone lines and the secure-upload link before the pilot fee is quoted, and keep the existing caveat text.

claims_checked.claim: RingReady: "$39 flat per month", "no setup fees, no contracts", "Unlimited calls on every plan", page also says "Starts at $39"; insurance AI receptionist that captures line of business, books consultations, forwards calls, texts/emails a summary.

Awava: AI Pro $1,997 one-time setup + $397/mo; AI Receptionist $97/mo on Website or Core; Core $1,297 setup + $297/mo; Website $2,497 one-time + $29/mo; month-to-month, 30 days' notice, setup fee charged once; "never quotes or binds".

Smith.ai: Free $0/mo for 25 calls ($3.00/call after); Pro $150/mo at $2.00 real call for 75 calls ($1.80 at 150, $1.67 at 300); Enterprise $500/mo at $1.67 for 300 calls ($1.60 at 500, custom at 1000+); month-to-month, 30 days' notice; custom prompting/integrations only on Enterprise.
Ruby receptionist plans $250/50 min, $395/100, $720/200, $1,725/500; chat plans $143/10 chats, $335/30, $520/50; "no additional or hidden fees for activation, onboarding, setup, customization".
Structurely/21X: platform fee not published (Small Team / Large Team / Enterprise comparison only); usage "as low as" $0.07/min voice (BYOC), $0.02/message SMS, $0.02/AI email.

Bridge: $25 per user per month struck through, $35 per user per month; upper tier $65 "Call For Pricing" with automated call summaries, sentiment monitoring and AI coaching; Custom plan (API access, live chat, chatbot) with "20 User Minimum for Customization", price on request.
NJ customer service representatives (BLS 2025 via O*NET): median $47,740/yr and $22.95/hr; 10th percentile $35,520; 90th percentile $72,040.
Anthropic Claude Haiku 5.5: $0.10/MTok input, $0.50/MTok output up to 100k-token prompts, $0.50/$2.50 above 100k; Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 per MTok.
LLM usage arithmetic: 600 enquiries x 8k input tokens = 4.8M tokens (~$0.48 at $0.10/MTok) + 0.7M output (~$0.35 at $0.50/MTok) = under $1 raw, $3-$10 band with headroom.
Telnyx SMS: $0.004 per outbound message part + carrier fee; $0.004 inbound + carrier fee; example blended US carrier passthrough $0.0038/part; volume tiers above 100M parts; $0 platform fee.
Telnyx voice: inbound local from $0.0032/min, outbound local from $0.005/min, call recording $0.002/min with $0 storage, $0 platform fee.
Telnyx numbers: $1.00 per local number per month, +$0.10/mo to add SMS/MMS, emergency calling $1.5/mo per number; therefore $2.60 per number and $7.80 for three.

10DLC: $4.50 brand registration fee, $15 per campaign review, recurring $1.50/mo (low volume mixed) up to $10/mo for standard-volume use cases incl. Customer Care, billed three months initially then monthly; Telnyx passes carrier 10DLC fees at cost.
10DLC risk: US 10DLC local numbers require brand + campaign registration before outbound texting, and campaign registration requires a "Message Flow" description of how users opt in.
SMS running-cost arithmetic: 1,500 parts x ($0.004 + $0.0038) = $11.70/month.
DigitalOcean Basic Droplets: $6 (1 GiB/1 vCPU), $12 (2 GiB/1 vCPU), $24 (4 GiB/2 vCPU) per month.

Retell AI: published overall range $0.07-$0.31/min; voice infra $0.055/min; platform voices $0.015/min; Claude 5.5 Haiku $0.0032/min; telephony $0.015/min; Retell phone numbers $2.00/month; SMS $0.01/message.

Agency Revolution Forge forms: the customer experience team adds a webhook key (created in AgencyZoom's Web Lead Integration) to the specific nominated website forms, and you specify which key goes on which form; multiple keys per form allowed.
Agency Revolution webhook pointed at a third-party/non-AgencyZoom endpoint is NOT documented (plan marks it confirmed_in_docs false and makes the pilot conditional on it).

Bridge AMS360 integration is a documented Bridge-side setup: AMS360 Web Service API user, then Bridge Settings > Agency Setup > Integration Setup with username/password/Agency ID/version; Open Client on Call/Answer screen pop, automatic activity export, and an AMS360 Notification Service feed.
Third-party write-back into Bridge/AMS360 from the consultancy's service is NOT documented, and API access appears only on the Bridge Custom plan (price on request).
Google Calendar API events.insert exists as POST https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{calendarId}/events (plan cites POST /calendar/v3/calendars/{calendarId}/events).
Google Calendar API quotas: 10,000 requests/min per project, 600/min per user per project, 1,000,000 requests/day billing threshold before charges apply.
Cal.diy is the MIT-licensed community edition relaunched by Cal.com, "only for self-hosting and use at your own risk".

N.J.A.C. 11:17A-1.3: a single act of soliciting/negotiating/selling requires a producer licence; no licensed producer may permit an unlicensed person to transact; subsection (e) covers employees who communicate directly with the public by mail, fax, computer or telephone.

FCC 24-17 (CG Docket 23-362, adopted Feb 2 2024, released Feb 8 2024) confirms the TCPA's "artificial or prerecorded voice" restriction encompasses current AI-generated human voices and requires prior express consent absent an exemption.

FTC Safeguards Rule (16 CFR 314) requires a written information security program, a designated Qualified Individual, risk assessment, encryption, MFA, service-provider oversight and incident response; the guide's list of 13 financial-institution examples does not name insurance agencies (plan flags coverage as inference).
N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-4(d): interception by a party, or with one party's prior consent, is lawful unless used to commit a criminal, tortious or other injurious act - i.e. New Jersey one-party consent.

NJ DOBI Bulletin 25-03 is addressed to "ALL INSURERS AUTHORIZED OR ADMITTED IN NEW JERSEY", requires a written AIS Program, and section 1.8 covers AI Systems "whether developed by the insurer or a third-party vendor" (plan flags any downstream producer obligation as inference).

NJDPA (P.L.2023, c.266): applies at 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers plus revenue from selling personal data; section 10 exempts GLBA Title V financial institutions and insurance institutions subject to C.17:23A-1 et seq.

suggested_pricing arithmetic: $550 x 12 = $6,600 = ~28% of $23,868 and ~11% of $59,670; $4,500 over 14-18 founder-days = ~$250-$321/day; $2,500 is ~1.25x Awava's $1,997 and $4,500 is ~2.25x it; Bridge uplift $65-$35 = $30 x 17 staff = ~$510/month.
Build-plan effort sums: phases 0-3 (2-3, 3-4, 6-7, 3-4 founder-days) = 14-18 founder-days, i.e. ~3-3.5 weeks before a 4-week pilot.
